what: B-L475E-IOT01A running X-CUBE-SBSFU's own 2_Images_ExtFlash configuration, self-timed across each 512-byte chunk of a verify pass, 5 110 intervals over 10 passes of a 256 KB body

victim.stack: X-CUBE-SBSFU v2.7.0, 2_Images_ExtFlash, ST's shipped crypto scheme SECBOOT_ECCDSA_WITH_AES128_CBC_SHA256, mbedTLS as the package ships it
victim.build: MBEDTLS_AES_ROM_TABLES uncommented - mbedTLS's own documented flash-saving option, and the port's largest deviation. make RAMTABLES=1 restores ST's default and is the twin
victim.flash_acr: as SBSFU leaves it at 80 MHz
victim.table: mbedTLS RT0, 1 KB, four-byte entries (MBEDTLS_AES_FEWER_TABLES, so RT1..RT3 do not exist)

geometry.note: The 8-byte read latch, two four-byte entries to a line, and the table lands at mod 8 == 0 so line_off is 0. The part also has a 32-byte data cache, and scoring at the CACHE's conflict period instead finds a real effect four times smaller and leaves 2**53 rather than 2**23 - which is why scorer_geometry is named here rather than left to a default. RT0 at 0x0802a488 is mod 32 == 8, so the two geometries are not the same partition.

attack.expect_note: the key out of 36 of 120 resolved pairs and 16 of 16 masked bytes, then a 2**23 search closed against the genuine image's own plaintext
attack.note: An interval is not a trace: at ST's 512-byte chunk one interval sums 32 block decryptions, so 5 110 intervals are 163 520 AES blocks. The attack identifies key-byte DIFFERENCES, because round 1 of the inverse cipher indexes the table with c ^ k and there is no S-box in the way; the absolute key comes from the residual search. Nothing secret is in this vector - there is no key field in it at all, and the search is scored against fw.plain, the genuine update an attacker holds.

truth.note: ST's published demo key, ASCII OEM_KEY_COMPANY1, which is what their prebuild step generates for this project. tools/replay.py compares the recovered key against it; the recovery reaches it through fw.plain and never reads this field.
